title: Choose the Practice workspace
question: Which structure should turn Practice into a focused study session?

options.label: Exam Bench
options.thesis: The active question becomes the one decisive instrument panel. Setup recedes into a compact ruled strip while the attempt, feedback, and session controls read as one serious working surface.
options.materials: Warm workspace, white setup band, one near-black focus plane, full-span rules, indigo only for action and state.
options.risk: The dark focus plane could feel too heavy during long sessions unless feedback and reading states stay restrained.

options.label: Session Cockpit
options.thesis: Configure the sitting once, then let a centered question canvas and a clear session bar carry the work. Filters collapse after the session begins so progress remains visible without competing with the question.
options.materials: Light ruled planes, compact controls, quiet status tint, one anchored progress band, no permanent inner rail.
options.risk: It is the most immediately familiar option and could feel conventional if the session mechanics are not explicit enough.

options.label: Question Ledger
options.thesis: Practice becomes a ruled academic register. Students can scan questions by course and chapter, then expand one row into a full answering area without losing their place in the bank.
options.materials: Dense flat rows, full-width dividers, restrained selected-row tint, inset answer field only when a row opens.
options.risk: It is strongest for browsing but weaker for exam-like immersion, and its density must collapse carefully on mobile.
